LESSON: WORK DONE AT HOME

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Our Home
Topic 3.2: Work Done at Home
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Work Done at Home, part of Our Home in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do people work?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Work Done at Home together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Creativity and imagination: learner enhances creativity and originality through role playing work done at home.

Values:
• Unity: learner enhances non-discrimination when appreciating work done at home during discussions.

• Responsibility: learner enhances hard work when picture reading different work done at home.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Developmental perspective: learner enhances ability to make the right choices when role playing work done at home.

Link to other learning area:

Work done at home enhances and relates to vocabulary of terms used in a home in Language Activities.

50

Suggested Learning Resources:

Video clips, charts, name cards, and pictures about work done at home, theme-based multi-purpose Communication Board,

adapted digital devices, songs and poems about work done at home, universal cuffs with padded pencils, crayons with grips,

paintbrushes with enhanced grip, slant boards, foot-boards for learners using lower extremities, book holders and page turners,

house moulds, non-chlorofluorocarbon based paints, clay/ papier-mâché or plasticine, positioning/ seating devices whose

worktops/ table tops are at a suitable height, mobility devices such as wheelchairs/ crutches

Related Service Providers: Physiotherapist, Occupational Therapist, Learner Support Assistant/ Scribe
